facts.value: Healthy fats are necessary and beneficial for health. Avoid trans fats and limit saturated fats from sources like red meat, butter, cheese, ice cream, coconut, and palm oil.
facts.programme_association: Healthy Lifestyles and Fitness Science Degree | ASU Online

facts.value: The majority of protein should come from plant sources like lentils, beans, nuts, seeds, and whole grains. Avoid processed meats like bacon.
facts.programme_association: Healthy Lifestyles and Fitness Science Degree | ASU Online

facts.value: Eat mostly vegetables, fruits, and whole grains.
facts.programme_association: Healthy Lifestyles and Fitness Science Degree | ASU Online

facts.value: Drink water. Consume sugary beverages, juices, and milk only in moderation. 100% fruit juice is high in calories.
facts.programme_association: Healthy Lifestyles and Fitness Science Degree | ASU Online

facts.value: Pay attention to salt intake from commercially prepared foods; most dietary salt comes from processed foods, not from added salt during cooking or at the table.
facts.programme_association: Healthy Lifestyles and Fitness Science Degree | ASU Online

facts.value: Vitamins and minerals must be obtained from food and are provided by a diet containing healthy fats, healthy protein, vegetables, fruit, milk, and whole grains.
facts.programme_association: Healthy Lifestyles and Fitness Science Degree | ASU Online

facts.value: The type of carbohydrates in the diet is more important than the amount. Good sources include vegetables, fruits, beans, and whole grains. Avoid sugared sodas, 100% fruit juice, and highly processed foods.
facts.programme_association: Healthy Lifestyles and Fitness Science Degree | ASU Online

facts.value: The guide recommends staying active and maintaining a healthy body weight.
